summary.headline: Music Broadcast Q1 FY27 revenue fell 10% YoY to INR44.5 crore, but EBITDA rose to INR8.9 crore (20% margin) on 26% lower opex.
summary.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR44.5 crore, down 10% YoY from INR49.3 crore but up 9% QoQ, with core radio at INR35.5 crore and creative business at INR9.8 crore. Total operating expenses fell 26% YoY to INR35.6 crore, lifting operating EBITDA to INR8.9 crore from INR0.9 crore a year ago. Reported PAT was INR9.2 crore against a loss of INR2.2 crore, helped by other income of INR8.2 crore. Management said Q2 has started softer, and the company is focused on revenue growth while cost savings are considered largely complete.

segments.name: Core radio
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR35.5 crore, up from INR34 crore in Q4 FY26. Management said pure radio advertising remains subdued.

segments.name: Creative (Radio Plus)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR9.8 crore, described as a strong rebound. Management sees traction in solution selling and on-ground activations and events.

guidance_outlook: Management said Q2 is historically weaker and has begun on a softer note.
Management is 'cautiously optimistic' and aims for sustained margin expansion through disciplined execution.
Rajiv Shah said most cost savings are done and current cost per quarter is at an optimum level.
Management said seasonality applies: H1 is about 45% of annual business and H2 about 55%.
Management said government spends are hard to predict because they depend on elections and topicality.
capex_capacity: Studios moved to a hub-and-spoke model, with offices shifted to co-working spaces, reducing premises cost.
Manpower was reduced by around 20%; management says the company is now at optimal headcount.
Nothing is currently in the pipeline for new horizontal or vertical ventures.
No buyback plans; cash is being held on the balance sheet.
demand_pricing: Share of top 25 radio spenders rose to 21.8% from 15.6% in Q4 FY26.
New clients make up 29% of new business coming into radio; about 20% of new business each quarter, with 80% from recurring advertisers.
FCT/non-FCT split was 78:22; market share stated as 25%.
Advertisers are shifting spend toward Radio Plus (creative) rather than pure radio, per management.
Government business is treated as a separate vertical that the company is trying to grow its share in.

qa_highlights.question: Further cost savings possible over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Shah said most savings are done and the current quarterly cost level is optimal.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a shift in ad spend from traditional FMCG to new-age advertisers?
qa_highlights.answer: Abraham Thomas said pure radio is subdued while Radio Plus is seeing traction, so the advertiser mix is shifting slightly, but the combination should help reach targets.

qa_highlights.question: Digital share, new client mix and industry outlook given the news ban?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is lobbying government for news and current affairs permission, and meanwhile is cutting costs and selling solutions. Digital is 4% of revenue and new clients are 29% of new radio business.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR400-450 million quarterly run rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said seasonality applies (H1 about 45%, H2 about 55%) and that it aims to maximise share of spend, without giving a number.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback given cash of INR200-plus crore and market cap near that level?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Shah said there are no buyback plans and cash is being held.

qa_highlights.question: Will impairment continue after FY26 impairment of INR49 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Shah said the FY26 impairment reflected weak revenue and a share price drop to INR4.5. Share price is now about INR6.4, and no further impairment is expected if performance holds, to be checked at year-end. The share price is still below book value, so there will be no impairment gain.

risks_watch: Q2 has started on a softer note, and pure radio advertising is subdued.
Government ad spend is volatile and hard to forecast, and news and current-affairs broadcast permission is still pending.
Revenue is still 10% lower YoY; EBITDA and PAT gains depend on cost levels holding and on revenue recovery.
Other income of INR8.2 crore contributed materially to PAT; the core operating profit before tax was INR4.1 crore.
Impairment risk remains tied to market price and year-end performance; the share price is below book value.
Digital share is only 4% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management highlights sequential growth and profitability gains, but flags a softer start to Q2, subdued pure radio demand, and unpredictable government spend. Answers on buyback and impairment were brief and noncommittal.
key_quotes: The first quarter of FY27 marked a positive start to the year with the company delivering sequential revenue growth and a significant improvement in profitability.
While Q2 is historically a weaker quarter and it has begun on a softer note.
So I think we have done most of the cost savings, and this should be an optimum level of cost per quarter that you are looking at.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 10% YoY to INR44.5 crore and management gave no numeric revenue guidance; Q2 has started softer, pure radio ad spend is subdued, and no capacity additions or new ventures are in the pipeline, so growth is unbacked. EBITDA growth is not comparable in % terms (INR0.9 crore base to INR8.9 crore) and is driven by cost cuts that management says are largely complete.
